No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result.

nominations.title: Automated Left Ventricle Strain Analysis from DENSE MRI
nominations.authors: Mohammad Naqizadeh Jahromi, Ariel J. Hannum, Zhan-Qiu Liu, Daniel B. Ennis, Dazhong Wu, Luigi E. Perotti
nominations.abstract: Background: Quantifying myocardial strains from Displacement ENcoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) MRI provides insight into left ventricular performance, but current data processing pipelines remain limited in automation, robustness, and full left ventricle coverage. Methods: We present a fully automated framework for voxel-wise displacement and strain analysis of the left ventricle from DENSE MRI. Our method integrates a multi-channel nnU-Net model trained on both magnitude and phase images for segmentation, an automated phase unwrapping approach, an adaptation of the regularized spatiotemporal least squares (RSTLS) formulation for displacement computation, and strain calculations based on radial basis function interpolation. The proposed framework enables the estimation of displacements and strains across the left ventricle from a full stack of short-axis images. Results: Validation using a computational phantom shows the framework's overall resilience to data noise. Following computational phantom evaluation, the proposed framework is applied to analyze DENSE MRI short-axis slices acquired in forty-seven (N=47) healthy volunteers and covering the full left ventricle. Circumferential, longitudinal, and radial strains are presented throughout the cardiac cycle and at peak systole, showcasing the performance of the proposed framework. Results show that circumferential and longitudinal strains are computed accurately. However, challenges persist when estimating radial strain, especially in the subendocardial layer. A group-wise strain comparison is also performed based on volunteers' sex and age showing a significant effect of sex on circumferential and longitudinal strains. Conclusions: Overall, the proposed framework provides an automated and modular pipeline to compute displacements and strains from DENSE MR images that can be scaled and generalized toward clinical applications.

nominations.title: Beyond AUC: Do Mammography Risk Models Predict When Cancer Occurs?
nominations.authors: Svetlana Krasnova, Andrey Krylov, Dmitry Sorokin
nominations.abstract: Longitudinal deep learning models for mammography-based breast cancer risk prediction output either per-year cumulative risks or a discrete distribution over the year of diagnosis, from which cumulative risks F1,...,F5 are derived. These models are evaluated almost exclusively with year-wise AUCs and the concordance index. We show that these metrics are largely insensitive to when cancer occurs: they can be high even for a model that carries no information about the year of diagnosis. We re-evaluate two recent longitudinal models (OA-BreaCR, LMV-Net) on CSAW-CC with a 5-year horizon using timing metrics computed on cancer cases only. Despite C-indices up to 0.75, neither orders cancer cases by time to diagnosis significantly better than chance (c_time 0.51 and 0.55, both 95% CIs covering 0.5). Weighted absolute timing error favours a constant "year 3" prediction over both models, so we use c_time as the primary timing metric. For Mirai's additive-hazard head, also used by LMV-Net, we analyse how per-year increments passed through a ReLU can collapse under severe class imbalance. We also propose a breast-level, two-stage model that separates whether from when. It matches LMV-Net in discrimination (C-index 0.745 vs. 0.746) but orders cancer cases better (c_time 0.58 vs. 0.51, paired 95% CI of the difference 0.01-0.13), on par with Mirai's published weights (0.57).

nominations.title: Non-Uniform Array Configuration and Antenna Deactivation for Energy-Efficient Sensing
nominations.authors: Parisa Ramezani, Meesam Jafri, Marina Petrova, Emil Bj{\"o}rnson
nominations.abstract: This paper proposes a non-uniform array design framework for energy-efficient multi-target sensing by jointly optimizing the antenna configuration and the transmit covariance matrix (TCM). To begin with, a limited number of antennas are selected from a set of antenna locations to maximize the minimum mainlobe-to-peak-sidelobe-level ratio (MMPSR) over a sensing region. Next, the antenna configuration is optimized using a simulated annealing (SA)-based search, while a TCM optimization problem is formulated using Charnes-Cooper transformation and solved as a convex semidefinite program for each fixed configuration. Subsequently, an adaptive antenna deactivation strategy is developed to determine the maximum number of antennas that can be switched off while satisfying an MMPSR requirement. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed non-uniform array design outperforms fixed uniform and non-uniform array benchmarks and requires fewer active antennas to achieve a required sensing performance, thereby supporting energy-efficient sensing.

nominations.title: Joint RF-VLP Position and Velocity Tracking: Bayesian Estimation and Performance Analysis
nominations.authors: Chaedam Son, Si-Hyeon Lee
nominations.abstract: Visible light positioning (VLP) provides accurate indoor positioning through optical received signal strength (RSS) measurements, while radio-frequency (RF) delay and Doppler measurements offer complementary range and velocity information. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate joint RF--VLP position and velocity tracking, addressing both recursive state estimation and its fundamental performance characteristics. We formulate a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem that combines optical RSS, RF delay and Doppler measurements, and motion prediction, and develop a Gauss--Newton-based algorithm for recursive tracking. To characterize the estimation limits and the benefits of RF--VLP integration, we derive the Bayesian information matrix and the corresponding Bayesian Cram\'er--Rao lower bound (BCRLB). We further introduce a state-conditioned information matrix (SCIM), whose inverse coincides with the MAP estimator's mean-squared error matrix under a first-order observation model, enabling tractable analysis of RF-induced information gains. The analysis quantifies the distinct contributions of RF delay and Doppler measurements and reveals different asymptotic estimation-error behaviors with respect to RF and VLP signal-to-noise ratios. Numerical results demonstrate improved position and velocity tracking over the considered baselines, with substantial velocity gains from RF sensing. The results also validate the theoretical asymptotic predictions and show that the inverse of the SCIM closely captures the estimator's error trends.

nominations.title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants
nominations.authors: Asif Iftekhar Omi, Anyu Jiang, Han Wu, Sultan Mahmud, Mali Halac, Shreyas Sen, Shriya Srinivasan, Adam Khalifa, Baibhab Chatterjee
nominations.abstract: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. A 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) prototype integrates a reconfigurable four-stage energy harvester with automatic stage selection and a tunable constant-current biphasic stimulator, achieving 63.5\% peak power-conversion efficiency (PCE) at $-16.3$ dBm and $>50\%$ PCE over a 9-dB input-power range. Preliminary in-vivo validation of DTCP was done with a second application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) on an injectable flexible substrate, capable of being delivered through a 14-gauge needle adjacent to the sciatic nerve of Sprague-Dawley rats (n=4). External copper-pad DTCP powering evoked repeatable hind-limb twitches and electromyography (EMG) response; ultrasound confirmed sub-millimeter nerve proximity, video-based paw-tip tracking captured the response, and 8-day post-implant dissection verified placement along the sciatic-nerve trajectory. Overall, this work provides an integrated wireless powering, energy-harvesting, and stimulation platform toward fully battery-free injectable neuromodulation implants.

nominations.title: Joint Movable Antenna Positioning and Precoding for ISAC via a Two-Timescale Model-Based GNN
nominations.authors: Alireza Fadakar, Yuchen Zhang, Andreas F. Molisch
nominations.abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) allow an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) to reshape multiuser channels and angular sensitivity. For monostatic multiuser communication and multi-target elevation and azimuth estimation, we minimize the expected target-averaged angular Bayesian Cram\'er-Rao bound (BCRB) subject to per-user block-level and long-term rate requirements. To avoid repeated online optimization, we propose a two-timescale model-based graph neural network (TT-MBGNN) over antennas, users, and targets. The slow policy selects positions from long-term statistics to reduce movement overhead, while the fast policy learns complex corrections to a regularized zero-forcing (RZF) reference using post-movement channels and target-angle priors. We jointly train both policies through a differentiable model of rates and BCRB, without optimization-generated labels. Across tested rate requirements, the network yields lower sensing bounds than variants using a fixed array, RZF, or both, with any-user fast-rate violations in 0.31-2.63% of test blocks. Frozen policies provide competitive sensing bounds for unseen user and target counts, and ten fine-tuning epochs improve communication reliability at higher user counts. Across tested network sizes, our framework achieves up to 3 dB lower BCRB than an idealized alternating-optimization benchmark that uses known target reflection coefficients. The network computes precoders approximately 50-fold faster in matched batch-one tests.

nominations.title: What Makes Good Datasets for Intelligent Multi-Modal Sensing-Communication Integration?
nominations.authors: Mingran Sun, Zengrui Han, Xuanyu Liu, Xuesong Cai, Xiang Cheng
nominations.abstract: Intelligent multi-modal sensing-communication integration, namely Synesthesia of Machines (SoM), represents an AI-native paradigm for enabling embodied intelligence and future wireless networks. Multi-modal sensing and communication foundation models developed for SoM learn cross-modal associations and generalizable environmental representations through large-scale pretraining, making the quality of pretraining datasets critical. However, existing methods lack unified evaluation of heterogeneous multi-modal data and thus struggle to meet the requirements for multi-modal pretraining dataset construction and selection. To bridge this gap, we introduce a comprehensive data evaluation framework for intelligent multi-modal sensing-communication integration. Specifically, we establish two complementary heterogeneous multi-modal data evaluation dimensions, including intrinsic data quality and validity, and model-based data utility. Furthermore, we present case studies to validate the effectiveness of the two evaluation dimensions. We also extend our analysis to investigate the impact of data quality on pretraining scaling laws and explore the value of integrating measurement and simulation data. Finally, we outline promising directions for future research on data evaluation.

nominations.title: Sensing with OFDM Signals: How Do the Constellations Affect the Sensing Accuracy?
nominations.authors: Junjie Chen
nominations.abstract: This paper investigates how communication constellations affect joint range-velocity estimation with data-bearing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. To this end, starting from the continuous-time sensing process, we derive a discrete observation model and specify its validity conditions. For multiple targets with unknown delays, Doppler shifts, and complex gains, the complete Fisher information matrix (FIM) admits a structural factorization separating deterministic channel derivatives from random symbol-energy weights. This structure yields a Jensen-type lower bound on the average conditional Cramer-Rao bound (CRB), which is attained exactly by constant-modulus constellations. Single-target closed-form expressions further reveal the dependence of the bounds on the transmitted energy distribution and physical OFDM parameters. We also formulate two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT), concentrated maximum-likelihood (ML), and sliding-subarray multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing under the derived observation model. Numerical results support the theoretical optimality of constant-modulus constellations but also show that the CRB gap between phase-shift keying (PSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) becomes negligible when the numbers of subcarriers and OFDM symbols are considerably large. The performance of ML estimation closely approaches the derived bounds, which confirms the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis. FFT processing exhibits grid-induced error floors. In the considered scenarios, MUSIC provides lower estimation errors than FFT and exhibits a more pronounced constellation dependence.

nominations.title: Active-Element Configuration for Energy-Efficient Secure Near-Field ISAC With Hybrid RISs
nominations.authors: Ling Zhuang, Ximing Xie, Fang Fang, Zhizhong Zhang
nominations.abstract: Hybrid active-passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (HRISs) are promising for secure near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) through selective signal amplification and spherical-wave beam focusing. However, fixed active-element layouts limit flexibility in exploiting element-dependent near-field channels while balancing secrecy performance, sensing accuracy, and circuit power consumption. This paper develops a joint active-element configuration and transmission design for a large-aperture HRIS-assisted system, where sensing targets act as potential eavesdroppers. The design adapts both the number and spatial distribution of active elements by exploiting near-field phase and attenuation variations. We establish a bidirectional signal and power model with full-aperture reflection and active-subset amplification for downlink signals and uplink echoes. Based on the derived three-dimensional localization Cram\'er-Rao bound, we formulate a mixed-integer non-convex secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem under user-rate, localization, and power constraints. To solve this problem, we propose an alternating optimization framework combining successive convex approximation, a penalty convex-concave procedure, and full-aperture reweighted group-sparse selection. The selection method scores and ranks elements to generate binary candidate configurations without exhaustive search. After refining continuous HRIS variables for each candidate, we select the feasible configuration with the highest genuine SEE. Simulation results demonstrate higher SEE with lower base station transmit power than fixed-layout HRIS schemes and a fully passive RIS baseline.

nominations.title: DyTransRM: A Unified Simulation-to-Real Framework for Dynamic Radio Map Prediction
nominations.authors: Simin Wang, Jiayi Wei, Jihong Li, Guhan Zheng, Rui Cheng, Shunqin Zhang
nominations.abstract: Dynamic radio map (RM) prediction enables proactive wireless network control by forecasting future propagation conditions from historical observations. However, collecting temporally continuous and spatially dense real-world RMs is prohibitively expensive, while models trained on large-scale simulated data often suffer from limited transferability to real environments. To address this issue, we propose DyTransRM, a unified simulation-to-real framework for dynamic RM prediction under sparse real-world measurements. DyTransRM first introduces RadioCLIP to learn physics-semantic representations by aligning environmental evolution with the corresponding propagation evolution, thereby improving both prediction accuracy and cross-domain transferability. To further bridge the simulation-to-real gap, SparseUOT employs sparse-mask simulation refinement to mimic realistic measurement patterns and unbalanced optimal transport to selectively align compatible propagation representations across domains. Experiments on RadioMapMotion and real-world datasets demonstrate that RadioCLIP achieves an NMSE of 0.0018 and an RMSE of 0.012 in simulation-domain prediction. After sparse real-domain adaptation, DyTransRM achieves an NMSE of 0.023, RMSE of 0.079, and MAE of 0.064, outperforming representative adaptation baselines without requiring spatially complete real RMs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DyTransRM for transferring simulation-learned dynamic propagation knowledge to practical sparse-measurement scenarios.

nominations.title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
nominations.authors: Mario Edoardo Pandolfo, Kyriakos Stylianopoulos, George C. Alexandropoulos, Paolo Di Lorenzo
nominations.abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

nominations.title: Hermitian Positive Definite Neural Networks for Matrix-CFAR Geometric Signal Detection in Nonhomogeneous Clutter
nominations.authors: Xiyao Chen, Takumi Sato, Linyu Peng
nominations.abstract: Matrix information geometry (MIG) detectors exploit the Riemannian geometry of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrices to achieve robust object detection in nonhomogeneous clutter. The matrix constant false alarm rate (matrix-CFAR) method is a representative MIG detector that relies on the geometric structures with respect to specific metrics. In most cases, computing representative HPD covariance matrices requires numerical methods, typically involving computationally intensive iterative optimization algorithms. Although explicit formulas are available for certain cases, such as the log-Euclidean (LE) mean, they are generally unavailable for many other matrix means and medians. To address this challenge, we propose integrating the Hermitian positive definite neural network (HPDNet) into the matrix-CFAR framework, replacing conventional numerical optimization procedures with a learned, geometry-preserving mapping that directly estimates representative HPD covariance matrices from data. In the simulations, the framework is evaluated for MIG detectors using both means and medians associated with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric, the LE metric, and the Bures--Wasserstein metric, on both simulated compound-Gaussian clutter and real IPIX sea clutter. In both cases, the HPDNet is trained solely on simulated data to assess its applicability to the study of real data. The results show a significant reduction of computational cost in testing, while maintaining detection performance and robustness.

nominations.title: Wideband Hybrid Beamforming via Programmable Unitary Mixer--TTD RF Networks
nominations.authors: Nikola Zlatanov, Damir Salakhov, Zhen Gao
nominations.abstract: This paper proposes a wideband hybrid beamforming architecture whose analog front-end consists of fixed unitary mixers interlaced with programmable diagonal phase-shift/true-time-delay (TTD) layers. Under ideal passive-component assumptions, the analog beamformer is semi-unitary on every OFDM subcarrier, so the injected RF-chain power reaches the antenna ports without analog-network loss. We design the phase shifts and delays of the programmable diagonal phase-shift/TTD layers for OFDM sum-rate maximization. Numerical results show that increasing mixer--TTD depth improves the sum rate under ideal component assumptions and a common injected RF-power budget. With component losses included, a shallow design retains an advantage over the evaluated hybrid baselines at low-to-moderate powers, motivating deeper implementations with low accumulated loss.

nominations.title: SWAN-Rx: Efficient and Bandwidth-Scalable Neural Reception for MIMO-OFDM
nominations.authors: Zhoubin Kou, Cong Shen
nominations.abstract: We present a Scalable Windowed Axial-attention Neural Receiver (SWAN-Rx) for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. The receiver improves reception accuracy and reduces forward-pass computation while supporting frozen-weight reuse across bandwidth allocations and channel conditions. It combines a common resource-element representation of received observations and pilot context with alternating time-axis and local frequency-axis attention. Shared parameters and relative positional information permit soft detection across allocation lengths without inference-time parameter updates. At fixed subcarrier spacing, model configuration, and symbol count, bounded frequency neighborhoods give linear growth of forward-pass computation with bandwidth. Evaluations compatible with the 5G New Radio physical layer reuse weights trained on four physical resource blocks (PRBs) at up to 273 PRBs and on unseen channels. At the training bandwidth, SWAN-Rx achieves lower pre- and post-decoding bit error rates than the implemented three-step neural receiver (NRX) and DeepRx-MIMO baselines, with 16.9% and 39.7% fewer parameters and 56.3% and 35.7% fewer forward-pass operations, respectively. The same weights achieve lower pre-decoding error rates than these baselines throughout the evaluated bandwidth-extrapolation and 16-PRB channel-transfer tests, with an estimated 0.4-0.9 dB signal-to-noise ratio reduction relative to NRX at a pre-decoding error rate of $10^{-2}$ in the 16-PRB tests.

nominations.title: Density-First Design of Anti-Jamming Sparse Spreading Codes for NB-IoT
nominations.authors: Michel Kulhandjian, Hovannes K. Kulhandjian, Daniel J. Jakubisin, Theodoros A. Tsiftsis, Alexandros-Apostolos A. Boulogeorgos
nominations.abstract: As narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) systems continue to be deployed in increasingly heterogeneous and demanding wireless environments, including those characterized by interference, high mobility, and potentially hostile conditions, enhancing the resilience of the physical-layer waveform has become an important and timely design consideration. Motivated by this need, the present paper introduces a density-first framework for the design of anti-jamming sparse spreading codes in NB-IoT systems. Building on this framework, we propose a generalized method for constructing sparse codes that decouples column density from the conventional Alamouti-paired structure, thereby enabling both disjoint-support and deterministic code designs. In addition, we develop a generative machine-learning approach based on a variational autoencoder for synthesizing jamming-robust sparse spreading codes. To evaluate the performance of sparse spreading under conditions of additive white Gaussian noise, fading, and pulse jamming, we present a bit-error-rate (BER) analysis framework. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations, conducted across a wide range of density, channel, and jamming conditions, show that the performance of sparse spreading codes is determined primarily by column density rather than by optimization of code coefficients. In particular, highly sparse codes with disjoint support offer the greatest robustness to jamming while avoiding the unfavorable intermediate-density regime. Relative to the prior-art Alamouti-paired low-density spreading code, the recommended uniform-density design reduces pulse-jamming BER by roughly 5 times; a deterministic Lempel-Costas construction attains the empirical optimum in closed form, while the variational-autoencoder generator yields a further 45% improvement over the best algebraic design.

nominations.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Lookup Table Demappers for Amplitude Phase-Shift Keying over Nonlinear Satellite Links
nominations.authors: K\"ur\c{s}at Tekb{\i}y{\i}k, G\"une\c{s} Karabulut Kurt, Antoine Lesage-Landry
nominations.abstract: Next-generation high-throughput satellites increasingly demodulate and decode on board, so the per-symbol cost of the receiver constrains payload power and throughput. Soft demappers for nonlinear satellite links must therefore produce accurate bit log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) at low cost. We introduce a KAN-LUT demapper, a two-layer Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN) whose learned univariate edge functions are stored as 128-entry lookup tables (LUTs), so that inference needs only table reads, linear interpolation, and additions. We bound the LLR error introduced by the tables and evaluate the demapper on amplitude phase-shift keying (APSK) links with low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding and a nonlinear traveling-wave-tube amplifier. For 16-, 32-, and 64-APSK, KAN-LUT stays within 0.2 dB of a per-cluster Gaussian log-MAP (LogMAP-CG) demapper, while its cost relative to LogMAP-CG falls from 87% to 27% as the order grows. It matches or slightly exceeds multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) at about one fifth of their cost, remains competitive under operating-point mismatch, and needs only tens of kilobytes of tables. KAN-LUT is therefore a low-cost candidate demapper for regenerative payloads.

nominations.title: Spatial phase coherence and its applications to masking and adaptive neighborhood sizing in multitemporal InSAR
nominations.authors: Magnus Heimpel, Irena Hajnsek, Othmar Frey
nominations.abstract: We examine spatial phase coherence (SPC), a measure of the correlation between the wrapped phase time series of two pixels in a stack of single-look synthetic aperture radar acquisitions. A pixel and its adjacent neighbors share speckle through the point spread function, so that decorrelation alone does not lower their SPC below a floor. We find that masking pixels whose mean SPC to their eight neighbors is well below that floor, as in parts of layover and shadow areas, is an inexpensive complement to geometry-derived layover and shadow masks. For distributed scatterer pixels, averaging SPC over a fixed set of neighbors that share no speckle yields a proxy for the local coherence, the phase coherence indicator (PCI), that is available before the selection of statistically homogeneous pixels (SHPs). In phase estimation, averaging more pixels reduces noise but may also increase the bias in heterogeneous areas. To relax this trade-off, we propose to enhance SHP selection algorithms by scaling the search window size according to the PCI and truncating the set of selected pixels where a smaller nested set agrees clearly better with the phases at the center. In simulations of a TerraSAR-X and a Sentinel-1 stack with 44 and 79 acquisitions, we apply this adaptive neighborhood sizing (ANS) to established amplitude- and covariance-based SHP selection algorithms with thresholds that adapt to the PCI. Without ANS, the largest tested search window size has 13 to 29 % more phase linking error than the best of the tested sizes. With ANS, the largest window has the lowest error of the tested sizes, 11 % lower than that of the same selection at its best tested size without ANS. On a real TerraSAR-X stack, the mask based on SPC flags pixels in building shadows that a terrain model misses. On real Sentinel-1 stacks, ANS preserves dense fringes on a slowly deforming slope and in part on a fast landslide.

nominations.title: Cross-Subject Priors for Maximum a Posteriori Estimation of Latent Structure Influence Models in Motor-Imagery EEG With Few Trials
nominations.authors: Sagnik De, Anil Kumar Gupta
nominations.abstract: Coupled hidden Markov models such as the latent structure influence model (LSIM) describe how the sensorimotor rhythms of the two hemispheres evolve and interact during motor imagery, but subject-specific maximum likelihood (ML) estimates are unstable when few trials are available. This paper derives a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator for the LSIM whose conjugate prior equals the expected statistics of $\lambda$ pseudo-trials from a population model fitted to other subjects. The M-step remains in closed form, expectation maximization keeps its monotone ascent, and ML ($\lambda=0$) and the population model ($\lambda\to\infty$) are limiting cases. The prior strength was selected on 35 subjects of the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset and applied unchanged to 70 held-out subjects and to BCI Competition IV-2a. With $\lambda=1$ the held-out log-likelihood exceeded that of ML in 61 of 70 subjects (Holm-adjusted $p=9.1\times10^{-8}$) and in all 70 subjects with five training trials per class. A prior learned only from the PhysioNet data improved the held-out likelihood of all nine BCI IV-2a subjects at five trials per class and reduced the error of the joint transition matrix by 61%. Decoding accuracy did not improve ($p=0.17$). Cross-subject priors therefore stabilize few-trial dynamic models of motor-imagery EEG, but they do not improve decoding, which in these data relies mainly on structure shared across subjects.

nominations.title: ANNA: Attention-Free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation for Channel Estimation on Regenerative NTN Payloads
nominations.authors: Miguel Camelo Botero, Nina Slamnik-Krije\v{s}torac, Johann Marquez-Barja
nominations.abstract: Accurate deep learning (DL)-based channel estimation (CE) for non-terrestrial network (NTN) uplinks must meet the processing, power, and latency constraints of regenerative payloads. We propose Attention-free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation (ANNA), a lightweight architecture combining per-resource block (RB) pilot projection, convolutional neighborhood aggregation, and shared reconstruction, with dense-grid expansion only at the output. Evaluation against learned and classical estimators uses paired waveform-generated datasets with receiver frequency correction enabled and disabled. With correction enabled, 16-bit floating point (FP16) deployment on a 10 W Jetson Orin NX achieves 0.372 ms 99th-percentile (P99) latency and 2.15 dB lower mean normalized mean-squared error (NMSE) than the fastest learned baseline at 29.6% higher latency. Relative to the most accurate learned baseline, ANNA is 4.08 times as fast and consumes 80.5% less module energy per sample, with a 1.14 dB accuracy penalty. It meets the adopted 0.5 ms P99 target in all 100 benchmark runs, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-latency-energy trade-off for embedded uplink CE.

nominations.title: Multi-Library Feature Engineering and Statistically Validated Classification for Power Swing Detection and Stability Assessment
nominations.authors: Pallav Kumar Bera, Samita Rani Pani, Ranjeeta Patel
nominations.abstract: Faults occurring during power swings, and the evolution of a swing into an unstable condition, cause distance-relay maloperation and cascaded outages. This paper identifies faults, faults during power swings, and power swings, and distinguishes stable from unstable swings in a 9-bus WSCC system modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC. Three time-series feature libraries (tsfresh, TSFEL, and tsfeatures) are applied to the 3-phase relay voltages and currents, giving 3286 statistical, temporal, spectral, and fractal descriptors per event window. A two-step feature selection (Boruta all-relevant filtering followed by RFECV- and SHAP-guided minimal-optimal pruning) reduces the feature set to 18 compact, non-redundant features. 14 classifiers spanning linear, kernel/instance-based, probabilistic, neural, and tree-ensemble/boosting families are then benchmarked under repeated stratified cross-validation, with model differences assessed by a Friedman/Nemenyi omnibus-and-post-hoc test and a Nadeau--Bengio corrected paired t-test. Rotation Forest (ROF) identifies the three event types with 99.98% and SVM-RBF distinguishes stable from unstable swings with 97.97% balanced accuracy. The results show that automated, library-driven feature extraction combined with rigorous statistical model comparison achieves near-perfect discrimination while retaining feature-level interpretability through SHAP importance.

nominations.title: Joint Antenna Positioning and Dynamic Beam Tracking for MA-Enabled Full-Duplex Secure ISAC Systems: A Flow Matching DRL Approach
nominations.authors: Zhendong Li, Yujie Zhao, Jianle Ba, Zhou Su, Wen Chen
nominations.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) improves spectral efficiency but faces significant security challenges in dynamic wireless environments, where the potential eavesdropper is treated as the sensing target. This paper proposes a movable antenna (MA)-enabled full-duplex secure ISAC system that tracks the mobile eavesdropper while safeguarding both uplink and downlink transmissions. Specifically, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is employed to recursively estimate and predict the eavesdropper's state from radar echoes. Building on the estimated target state, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of the uplink and downlink secrecy rates by jointly optimizing the transmit and receive MA positions, uplink and downlink beamforming, artificial noise, and uplink transmit power. The resulting problem is challenging due to its inherent nonconvexity, strong coupling among optimization variables, and time-varying nature. Conventional iterative optimization methods may incur prohibitive computational overhead in dynamic environments, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods based on unimodal Gaussian or deterministic policies may struggle to capture complex multimodal high-reward action distributions. To address these challenges, we develop a flow matching-based deep reinforcement learning (FMDRL) algorithm for sequential joint decision-making. The proposed algorithm integrates a conditional velocity-field actor with twin critics, generating continuous actions through finite-step Euler integration and employing a deterministic decoder to enforce physical constraints on antenna positions, transmit power, and positive semidefiniteness. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed FMDRL algorithm achieves superior performance in terms of both communication security and target tracking capabilities.

nominations.title: Wideband Terahertz Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS): Bandwidth Limits, Ergodic Rate, and Placement Optimization
nominations.authors: Almutasem Bellah Enad, Chintha Tellambura, Zhiguo Ding
nominations.abstract: Terahertz (THz) bands offer the vast bandwidth that sixth-generation (6G) networks demand, but their severe path loss makes bringing the radiator close to the user decisive. Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) do exactly this, turning path loss into a programmable parameter by sliding radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, which makes THz their native regime. That regime, however, is inherently wideband and the waveguide is dispersive, whereas every existing PASS analysis is single-frequency and assumes a non-dispersive guide. This paper develops the first wideband, dispersion-aware theory of PASS and uncovers a limitation intrinsic to the pinching mechanism. Because co-phasing by physical position equalizes path length only modulo a wavelength, a pinching array is inherently beam-squint limited, and we show its frequency response is a Dirichlet kernel with a closed-form coherence bandwidth and an irreducible dispersion floor that even true-time-delay (TTD) correction cannot remove. A single unifying law governs the behavior, in which array gain trades against both coherence bandwidth and spatial robustness through one invariant that TTD correction breaks, reaching the floor with far fewer delay elements than a conventional array. We further characterize the wideband ergodic rate under random user locations, show that molecular absorption acts as a deterministic taper that multiplies the squint, and derive a simple rule for the rate-optimal number of pinches. Finally, by exploiting the integer structure of co-phasing, we recast the non-convex placement problem as a mixed-integer program that can be solved exactly in polynomial time. Together, these results move PASS from the narrowband, dispersion-blind setting to the wideband, dispersive regime that THz operation actually requires.

nominations.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
nominations.authors: Amritash Patra
nominations.abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = \gamma T, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes \chi_+ and \chi_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound \beta(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (\kappa_{T_1} = (3\pi - 8)/(3\pi + 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (\kappa_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound \kappa_\star = (\pi - 2\sqrt{2})/(\pi + 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit \pi swaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superconducting transmons and trapped-ion qubits, extend the analysis to finite damping, pulse dwell, colored thermal baths, and qutrit leakage, and construct two-branch differential lock-in protocols that isolate directional error splits immune to first-order state-preparation and measurement errors.

nominations.title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
nominations.authors: Sizhe Yan, Biao Wu
nominations.abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.

nominations.title: Optimal Frobenius light cones for power-law systems in any dimension
nominations.authors: Laura Shou, An Le, Twesh Upadhyaya, T. C. Mooney, Alexey V. Gorshkov
nominations.abstract: We prove optimal Frobenius Lieb-Robinson bounds for power-law systems with power-law exponent $\alpha$ in any dimension $d$, in particular showing that the algebraic to linear light cone transition occurs at $\alpha=d+1$. The proof uses a spectral clipping method and concentration result to allow for running a multiscale operator-norm argument which produces the optimal Frobenius norm exponent. Additionally, we prove there is a Frobenius light cone transition from polylogarithmic to algebraic at the summability threshold $\alpha=d$, and a transition from decaying in volume to non-decaying in volume at $\alpha=d/2$.

nominations.title: Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
nominations.authors: Adri\'an Mar\'in Boyero, Fynn Otto, Albert Rico, Otfried G\"uhne, Malte Lochau
nominations.abstract: A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. However, adapting metamorphic testing to the quantum realm is not straightforward, since quantum states cannot be directly inspected. We propose a framework of quantum metamorphic testing (QMT) in which the metamorphic relations incorporate the measurement procedures required to assess quantum outputs. We apply our QMT framework to testing the preparation of stabilizer states, which are central to protocols like measurement-based quantum computing or quantum error correction. We utilize structural properties of stabilizer states to systematically derive measurement circuits for new test cases from existing ones. We implement this framework in Qiskit, and demonstrate that it reduces by an order of magnitude the testing run time compared to testing with randomly generated input states. We further show effectiveness by revealing synthetic program faults injected by circuit mutations, as well as a real bug in the Qiskit compiler.

nominations.title: Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
nominations.authors: Mart\'i Cladera-Rossell\'o, Sebastian Horvat, Borivoje Daki\'c, Lee A. Rozema, Philip Walther
nominations.abstract: The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.

nominations.title: A Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem with Smooth Modulus
nominations.authors: Aparna Gupte
nominations.abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for the vector dihedral coset problem over $\mathbb{Z}_q^n$, in which the goal is to recover $\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ given independent samples of the form $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|{0,\mathbf{x}}\rangle+|{1,\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{s}}\rangle\bigr)$, for $\mathbf{x}\sim \mathbb{Z}_q^n$. When the modulus $q$ is $B$-smooth, the algorithm uses $n^{O(B^{1+o(1)}\log q)}B^{O(B^{2+o(1)}\log q)}$ samples and time. For $B = \mathrm{polylog}(n)$ and $q=\mathrm{poly}(n)$, this gives a quasipolynomial time- and sample-complexity. This extends the previously known quasipolynomial-time result for power-of-two moduli (Bonnetain, Naya-Plasencia, ASIACRYPT 2018; Bai, Jangir, Kirshanova, Ngo, Youmans, CRYPTO 2025). The algorithm proceeds by reducing the modulus one prime factor $p | q$ at a time. The key ingredient is a sieving procedure that clears the non-linear terms in the phase modulo $p$ via an algorithm of Ivanyos, Santha (TCS 2017) that finds non-zero $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{F}_p^\ell$ such that $\sum_{i \in [\ell]} u_i^d \mathbf{a}_i = 0 \mod p$ for degrees $1 \le d \le p-1$, given vectors $\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_\ell \in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ as input. The algorithm also applies to the extrapolated dihedral coset problem (EDCP) introduced by Brakerski, Kirshanova, Stehl\'e, Wen (PKC 2018), which is known to be equivalent to LWE in the polynomial sample regime. However, our result does not yield a new attack on LWE in any regime, precisely because the known reduction from LWE to EDCP provides only polynomially many clean samples, whereas our algorithm requires quasipolynomially many samples. The main algorithm was obtained in a GPT-5.6 Sol conversation prompted by the author; the author is responsible for all statements, proofs, and correctness. Concurrent work of Boucher, Fouque, Shen gives an algorithm with similar guarantees for prime-power moduli.

nominations.title: Double-Randomized Quantum Singular Value Transformations For Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
nominations.authors: Joel Bierman, Pawan Poudel, Yuan Liu
nominations.abstract: The Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) is an algorithmic framework which encompasses a wide range of problems, including Hamiltonian dynamics, ground state preparation, Gibbs state preparation, amplitude amplification, and matrix inversion. For many areas of scientific interest such as quantum chemistry and condensed matter, the circuit depth of the block-encoding subroutine in QSVT can be formidable, limiting the scope of problems to which QSVT can be applied on early fault-tolerant hardware. We split linear operators $A$ into a core operator $A_0$ and a tail operator $A_\epsilon$, block-encoding the normalized sum of $A_0$ and the average of $n_T$ randomly sampled terms from $A_\epsilon$. We show that using randomized block-encodings of this form allows one to lower the circuit depth of QSVT while incurring a diamond norm error that scales as $\mathcal{O}(C_P\delta^2/n_T$), where $C_P$ is a prefactor which depends on the QSVT polynomial $P$ and $\delta$ is the ratio of the $\ell_1$ norms of the coefficient vectors of $A_\epsilon$ and $A$. We then go on to show that if one samples QSVT circuits from a joint probability distribution of both random block-encodings and random polynomials (Double-Randomized QSVT), then the circuit depth savings of these two randomization techniques combine multiplicatively, with only additive error contributions. We numerically calculate error bounds for long-range Heisenberg and iron-sulfur complex Hamiltonians, showing that for a diamond norm error bound of $10^{-3}$, RBE-QSVT can reduce the number of Pauli terms needed for the block-encoding by an order of magnitude or more in several cases. This paves the way for demonstrations of QSVT on early fault-tolerant hardware.

nominations.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
nominations.authors: Avani Vivrekar, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen
nominations.abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.

nominations.title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
nominations.authors: Vicente Leyton-Ortega, Kathleen Hamilton
nominations.abstract: Whether a trained quantum generative model has learned its target is usually decided by a diagnostic validated on a labeled benchmark, and such a diagnostic can pass that validation by recovering how the benchmark was built. We analyze Fisher-trace and kernel-based certification of the real-amplitude quantum circuit Born machine in noiseless statevector simulation. For real-amplitude circuits built from half-angle rotations, the classical Fisher information equals the quantum Fisher information almost everywhere, so its trace equals the parameter count and carries no information about fit quality. The Fisher eigenvalue rank counts the live nodes of the amplitude tree: it coincides with the label on a sparse benchmark and is uninformative on a full-support one. The pooled Wasserstein and maximum-mean-discrepancy scores move with optimizer convergence and with the scoring convention. For two bitstring defect families on which both metrics have closed forms, we compute the tolerance-mismatch window in which the discrepancy rejects generators that the transport threshold admits; it opens only at certification-grade tolerances and closes as the qubit number grows. On the Hamming cost we prove a sharp tolerance ratio above which the discrepancy vote is redundant, and we obtain the exact worst-parity minimax value over all unit-diagonal positive-semidefinite kernels, which is exponentially small in the qubit number. In a numerical campaign at the tolerances a near-term experiment can resolve, the discrepancy vote changed no verdict at a thousand shots or more. The false-pass guarantee does not extend to device noise.

nominations.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
nominations.authors: William S. McGregor, Niclas Westerberg, Robert Bennett
nominations.abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

nominations.title: Quantum Coloring Games on Complete Graphs
nominations.authors: William Bolduc, Michael Jennings
nominations.abstract: We study the nonlocal game where two players are both given an input ($x$ and $y$, respectively), from a set of size $n$ and, without communicating, must give outputs $a$ and $b$, respectively, from a set of size $m < n$, winning when $(x = y) \leftrightarrow (a = b)$. This can be considered a graph coloring game on the complete graph with $n$ vertices. In the simplest case, the players get random equal inputs with probability $\frac{1}{2}$ and random unequal inputs otherwise. We solve this case of the game, and many others, for both classical and quantum (i.e., where the players may share finite-dimensional entangled quantum states) strategy sets, proving the value (the probability of winning) of the optimal strategies and providing explicit strategies that attain this optimum for all $n$ and $m$. Our optimal strategies are synchronous: i.e., the two players always give equal outputs when given equal inputs. These strategies remain optimal when the probability of receiving equal inputs is at least $\frac{2}{m + 2}$. Across this wide range of cases, we find that quantum strategies have an advantage over classical strategies exactly when $m$ does not divide $n$; this advantage is $O\left(\frac{m}{n^2}\right)$.

nominations.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
nominations.authors: Brian Barch, Luis Pedro Garc\'ia-Pintos
nominations.abstract: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cram\'er-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.

nominations.title: Control of Non-Markovianity via Channel Exceptional Points in a Driven-Dissipative Kerr-Cat Qubit
nominations.authors: Tian-Le Yang, Hao-Long Zhang, Pei-Rong Han, Zhen-Biao Yang, Shi-Biao Zheng
nominations.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems are conventionally defined at the Liouvillian level, making them representation-dependent and often requiring auxiliary degrees of freedom. We study EPs directly at the quantum-channel level in a driven-dissipative Kerr-cat qubit, in which dissipation drives bidirectional jumps between its two basis states. Interpolating two Markovian channels yields single EPs when the endpoints straddle a spectral-phase boundary and, remarkably, double EPs within the same phase. The interpolated EPs map out a Markovian--non-Markovian phase diagram: the parameter plane separates certified non-Markovian and Markovian domains, with domain boundaries switching the channel between the two characters. Three spectral criteria certify every domain. As the evolution time advances, the domains drift, split, and partially shrink, making the switching increasingly sensitive to parameters and time. This establishes a representation-independent paradigm for classifying and switching quantum memory effects, applicable to continuous-variable, discrete-variable, and hybrid systems.

nominations.title: Machine-learned active spaces enable quantum calculations of spin-state energetics of transition-metal complexes on quantum hardware
nominations.authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Sabre Kais, Werner Dobrautz
nominations.abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. The orbitals that belong in it are those that are strongly entangled in the correlated wavefunction, but measuring this entanglement requires the very correlated calculation that the active space is meant to make affordable. Here we present SpinAware, a machine-learning model that predicts density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution of each spin state, without any correlated calculation. Each of the 20 highest occupied and 20 lowest unoccupied orbitals is described by 60 descriptors computed from the UHF solution, among them the differences between its alpha and beta occupations and energies, its metal-d and ligand character, and its exchange coupling to the other orbitals, and a transformer predicts the entropy of each orbital in the context of all others. Trained on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations on mononuclear Cr-Ni complexes, the model transfers to experimentally characterized complexes with ligands, binding topologies, oxidation states and metals absent from training. Over 11 spin states it reproduces the DMRG entropy profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.027, and combining the predicted entropies with the predicted mutual information gives a candidate pool that contains 99% of the DMRG-active orbitals of the benchmark spin states while keeping, on average, only 15 of the 40 orbitals. Natural-orbital occupation scans then select compact active spaces from this pool for a nickel and a cobalt complex. Sample-based quantum diagonalization with samples from IBM quantum processors reproduces the exact CASCI energies of these spaces to within 0.3 kcal/mol and their spin-state gaps to within 0.10 kcal/mol for up to 32 qubits.

nominations.title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
nominations.authors: Liyi Li, Mahir Anand, James Bryan Graves, Amr Sabry
nominations.abstract: To find a $k$-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all $2^n$ subsets of the $n$ vertices, although only the subsets of size $k$ can be answers. We present ENQ+, an AQC language in which the programmer writes both cost functions. Data constraints define the problem cost function. Relational constraints, a new construct, declare the moves the search may make between configurations and define the initial cost function. For the clique, a single relational constraint, which exchanges a chosen vertex with an unchosen one, confines the search to the subsets of size $k$. ENQ+ thereby turns constrained quantum annealing, which physicists set up by hand for individual problems, into a programming construct. We give ENQ+ a semantics in many-world configuration (MWC) graphs, whose nodes are configurations and whose edges are moves, and derive from it a step-wise semantics of adiabatic evolution. We prove that a run stays within the component of the MWC graph that contains its initial state, and that a run from an approximate initial state still reaches the answer, with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact one. We compile ENQ+ to quantum circuits, prove the compilation correct with respect to the semantics, and use ENQ+ to program the Three-Dimensional Matching, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Traveling Salesperson problems.

nominations.title: Efficient simulation of the generalized Langevin equation using a basis of dynamically relevant histories for memory and noise
nominations.authors: Dmitriy Kondaurov, Evgeny Polyakov
nominations.abstract: The Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) is a cornerstone for modeling non-Markovian dynamics, but its numerical solution remains challenging due to the history-dependent convolution and the need to generate colored noise with a prescribed correlation function. We introduce a forward construction that addresses both challenges within a single framework. We represent an arbitrary trajectory as sum of relevant and irrelevant parts, where relevant part can be decomposed into a small number of characteristic history patterns that make the main contribution to future dynamics. It allows to reduce numerical cost to \(O(d^2)\) for $d$ chosen patterns instead of full history. The same construction applies to colored noise generation, where the causal filter plays the role of the memory kernel. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method for several representative kernels, including long-range kernels with power-law tails.

nominations.title: Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
nominations.authors: Chenzewei Qing, Tengyu Zhang, Xiaoqin Luo, Xiaolu Su, Li You
nominations.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. Guided by these dynamical signatures, SCOPE explores multiple perturbed decoding trajectories in parallel, enabling early termination and reseeding within a fixed serial iteration budget, with message-passing parameters optimized offline by simulated annealing. Circuit-level simulations of the $[[144,12,12]]$ BB code yield a logical error rate of $p_L=4.82\times10^{-10}$ at a physical error rate of $p=10^{-3}$. We further realize a pipelined two-arm memory-augmented BP (Mem-BP) core at the register-transfer level. Functional simulations at a 250 MHz clock yield a 16 ns BP iteration interval per arm and a mean input-to-result latency of 173.8 ns at $p=5\times10^{-3}$.

nominations.title: Excitation-Selective Control of Protected Subradiant Antiresonances
nominations.authors: Jing Tang, Yuangang Deng
nominations.abstract: Subradiant cavity antiresonances exhibit narrow spectral features, yet controlling their nonlinear response without perturbing the protected resonance remains challenging. Here we demonstrate excitation-selective control of a subradiant antiresonance in a driven two-emitter cavity-QED system. An auxiliary collective channel leaves the antisymmetric single-excitation state unaffected while shifting the doubly excited state, introducing tunable excitation anharmonicity without altering the linear antiresonance. This separation enables control of two-photon excitation pathways and photon correlations. Independently, a spatial coupling phase tunes optical access to the subradiant state without changing its intrinsic decay rate. We find that the interferometric phase information per incident photon is optimized when cavity-induced readout approximately matches intrinsic subradiant decay, while steady-state atomic entanglement peaks at an intermediate coupling phase. We further extend phase-selective optical control to collective subradiant modes in correlated emitter arrays. These results establish collective symmetry and spatial mode matching as distinct controls of nonlinear photon correlations, optical phase information, and atomic entanglement.

nominations.title: Scalable and Interpretable Quantum Mixture of Experts for High-Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data
nominations.authors: Junghoon Justin Park, Anna Jung, Kyumin Lee, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Shinjae Yoo, Jiook Cha
nominations.abstract: Quantum Mixture of Experts (QMoE) architectures offer a promising path toward scalable quantum machine learning, yet existing approaches remain largely confined to low-dimensional benchmarks and often rely on naive input partitioning that disrupts feature dependencies. We address these gaps by introducing Feature-Partitioned QMoE, which partitions high-dimensional spatio-temporal inputs into functionally coherent feature groups and assigns each group to a dedicated quantum expert. We further propose a hierarchical interpretability framework that leverages the modular structure of QMoE to produce circuit-level gating analysis, per-expert gradient saliency, and heterogeneity-based subtype discovery. Applied to ADHD classification from resting-state fMRI (N=4,458, ABCD Study, 180 brain ROIs, 363 timepoints), the proposed Theory-Driven QMoE achieves performance comparable to matched-capacity classical and quantum baselines while enabling circuit-attributable interpretation. The framework identifies FDR-corrected ADHD-associated biomarkers in executive-control and anterior default-mode networks and reveals three neurobiologically meaningful ADHD subtypes. These results position Feature-Partitioned QMoE as a scalable and interpretable methodology for applying quantum machine learning to high-dimensional biomedical data.

nominations.title: Advancing Quantum Reinforcement Learning with Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search and Adaptive Non-local Observables
nominations.authors: Junghoon Justin Park, Kyumin Lee, Anna Jung, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Shinjae Yoo, Jiook Cha
nominations.abstract: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ans\"atze. Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) address these issues independently, but to our knowledge have not been combined or compared in a single QRL framework. We present an ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the Quantum Time-series Transformer (QTSTransformer), evaluated on a 2 x 2 factorial design across six environments--two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games. Three findings emerge. First, the quantum agent outperforms a matched classical transformer baseline on five of six environments, with absolute scores ranging from 360.0 vs 304.0 (MarioBros) to 17.2 vs 2.5 (Breakout), while using approximately 12.5x fewer transformer parameters on the four Atari environments (more modestly so on the two classic-control tasks). Second, ANO and DiffQAS provide complementary benefits: ANO yields the largest gain on continuous-state CartPole (347.7 vs 223.2), while DiffQAS yields the largest absolute Atari gains (Breakout 17.2 vs 3.0; DonkeyKong 70.0 vs 37.0). Third, combining both innovations exhibits an asymmetric interaction: ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS, whereas DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade when ANO is added. These results provide design guidance for QRL agents: select between ANO and DiffQAS according to whether the bottleneck is the measurement basis or the gate topology, rather than applying both indiscriminately.

nominations.title: Stargate: Security Analysis and Mission-Aware Firewall for the CubeSat Space Protocol
nominations.authors: Owen Ramsey, Carlos Gonzalez-Cortes, Efren Lopez-Morales
nominations.abstract: The CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) is widely used for communication in CubeSat missions, yet its security model and attack surface remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present a systematic security analysis of CSP and identify fundamental limitations in its trust assumptions, coarse-grained network abstractions, privileged management services, application command semantics, and lack of mission-context awareness. Based on these findings, we develop a taxonomy of CSP attacks spanning four classes: network identity abuse, management service abuse, application semantic abuse, and mission context abuse. We then introduce Stargate, a modular, mission-aware firewall that enforces CSP-specific policies derived from this taxonomy, including node and service authorization, command-level filtering, and mission-context constraints. We implement Stargate and evaluate it on a virtual testbed based on a real-world CubeSat mission and flight software. Stargate successfully blocks all 11 representative attacks across the four attack classes while introducing only 1.42 ms of additional median round-trip latency. Our results demonstrate that protocol- and mission-aware policy enforcement provides a practical approach for securing CSP-based spacecraft networks.

nominations.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
nominations.authors: Miguel A. Guirao Aguilera, Satyajayant Misra, Efren Lopez-Morales
nominations.abstract: AI agent interoperability protocols enable orchestrators to discover and invoke external agents using machine-readable metadata. In the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, Agent Cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields that may influence agent selection before a provider is invoked, creating a pre-invocation trust problem. We characterize this discovery-time attack surface through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks and present SECCARD, a layered validation framework combining protocol checks, deterministic analysis, and LLM-based semantic reasoning. We measure the emerging public A2A ecosystem by probing 36.1 million Internet domains and collecting 310 deployed Agent Cards. Two annotators independently label the corpus with 96.8% agreement. We then construct a 660-card real-card perturbation benchmark with matched benign controls and a 260-card synthetic adversarial benchmark spanning all ten attack categories. On controlled attacks injected into real Agent Cards, the strongest semantic judge achieves 97.0% security recall at a 1.7% false-positive rate. Across nine LLM judges on the synthetic benchmark, security recall ranges from 25.8% to 92.3%, demonstrating substantial model-dependent variation. These results show that SECCARD effectively identifies Agent Card manipulations spanning all ten discovery-time attack classes while preserving benign Agent Cards, but also reveal that its effectiveness depends critically on the choice of the underlying LLM judge.

nominations.title: Quantifying Membership Inference Risks in Genomic Data Sharing: The Role of Attacker's Auxiliary Information
nominations.authors: Maryam Ghasemian, Lynette Hammond Gerido, Erman Ayday
nominations.abstract: Genomic data sharing is essential for biomedical research but introduces significant privacy risks, including membership inference attacks, in which an adversary determines whether a specific individual's data was used in a study. Existing privacy protections are typically applied after a release format has already been chosen, leaving researchers without a principled method to assess dataset-specific risk beforehand. We propose a server-assisted, principal component analysis-based pre-release auditing framework that maps genomic data into a shared low-dimensional space, applies epsilon-local differential privacy via the Laplace mechanism with a formally derived sensitivity for principal component analysis scores, and estimates membership inference attack power at a controlled 5% false-positive rate using a distance-threshold attack. A membership-neutrality diagnostic based on Unbiased Reconstruction Robustness is reported alongside attack power, precision, and recall. Experiments using the openSNP and 1000 Genomes Project datasets across multiple dimensionalities and privacy budgets show that separation between the researcher's dataset and public auxiliary data in principal component analysis space is a dominant determinant of attack success, exceeding the effect of perturbation level alone. Comparison against a genome-wide association study-style likelihood ratio test baseline further contextualizes the measured risk. This framework enables researchers, data repositories, and institutional review bodies to quantify dataset-specific membership inference risk before genomic data publication, supporting more informed and privacy-aware biomedical data-sharing decisions.

nominations.title: Memory Safety Isn't All You Need: Code Reuse Attacks in Memory Safe Languages
nominations.authors: Eric Cornelissen, Musard Balliu
nominations.abstract: Memory safety rules out classical code reuse attacks that rely on arbitrary memory corruption, but does not eliminate code reuse altogether. Attacks such as object injection, prototype pollution, class pollution, DOM clobbering, and DOM script gadgets arise in memory-safe languages without violating the underlying memory safety abstraction. We show that these seemingly different attacks share a common structure: Attacker-controlled data influences accesses to shared runtime state, such as runtime type information, prototype or class state, and the DOM, and a value fetched from that state subsequently influences a security-sensitive operation. Drawing on this insight, we develop a language-agnostic framework that decomposes an attack into a weakness, ending in a fetch from shared runtime state, and a gadget, which propagates the fetched value to a sensitive sink. We show that the framework captures five established attack classes and use it to derive stateless, mutating, and recycling weaknesses, together with simple, vertical, and horizontal gadget structures. We further systematize existing defenses into three common strategies - mediation, minimization, and constraint - and use them to derive candidate defense directions. Finally, we develop a model language that gives a formal account of code-reuse weaknesses and potential conditions for gadgets and end-to-end vulnerabilities.

nominations.title: Privacy-Preserving Clustering Algorithm and Parameter Selection for Collaborative Population Stratification Using Distributed PCA
nominations.authors: Maryam Ghasemian, Lynette Hammond Gerido, Erman Ayday
nominations.abstract: We propose a privacy-preserving selection layer for collaborative population stratification workflows, enabling an honest-but-curious server to recommend a strong clustering algorithm-hyperparameter configuration from privacy protected shares. Instead of using a fixed workflow such as PCA followed by K-Means with a preset number of clusters, the framework compares multiple clustering methods and parameter settings under privacy constraints. To avoid relying on a public reference basis, we construct a shared low-dimensional representation through a distributed-PCA (DPCA) procedure in which each party computes local top-$r$ principal-component information and the server aggregates only low-rank summaries to recover a global basis. Building on this representation, the framework supports three LDP-protected pipelines: PCA then Noise, Noise then PCA, and Noise-Only. The server evaluates clustering methods and parameter settings using internal validation metrics and recommends a top-performing configuration from the perturbed data; this step is pure post-processing. Experiments on openSNP and 1000 Genomes show that the server-side selection layer reliably identifies strong settings from LDP-protected data. Across both datasets, the PCA-based pipelines outperform Noise-Only in clustering utility, communication cost, and runtime, and show lower membership-inference attack (MIA) power at small privacy budgets. Overall, they provide the best utility--scalability trade-off in our setting.

nominations.title: Agent-ZTA: A chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Bidirectional Security-State Propagation and Runtime Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation
nominations.authors: Asadullah Abdullah Khan, Toqeer Ali Syed
nominations.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly delegate tasks and permissions across chains of autonomous agents that invoke protected tools. Although agent identities and delegated credentials may remain valid throughout a workflow, the security condition of any agent along the chain can deteriorate during runtime execution-either through upstream compromise or downstream ingestion of untrusted inputs. Authorization models based solely on the immediate caller and its static delegated scope fail to account for these mid-execution state changes. This paper develops Agent-ZTA, a chain-aware Zero Trust authorization and containment model that links runtime security-state changes across multi-agent delegation graphs. The model distinguishes an agent's path-specific delegated authority bound from the effective permissions currently exercisable under trusted policy. It defines an architecture featuring independently enforced policy decisions, authenticated delegation provenance, a dynamic chain-state view, and explicit fail-safe handling of missing or stale authorization signals. Furthermore, Agent-ZTA defines bidirectional security state propagation, allowing downstream security events to affect relevant upstream workflow states, and specifies adaptive branch-scoped containment through restricted permissions and a sandbox ("jail") execution mode where an isolation boundary is available.
